items.title: George P. Fleming Interview, 1984-10-06
items.q: And it was Ernie Lewis. He'd become one of the executives for the Musicians' Union. And Wilbur Barranco, the late Wilbur Barranco. And Vernon Alley. All these guys I used to play with.

ctx.x: Oh, something else I would like to add to that. Doing those years with Ben Watkins, I also played with Jerome Richardson, which is one of the world's great alto players. And I have a picture of he and I at a jam session together. And it was Ernie Lewis. He'd become one of the executives for the Musicians' Union. And Wilbur Barranco, the late Wilbur Barranco. And Vernon Alley. All these guys I used to play with.

Well, I guess a few years ago, you somehow decided to go over to the New Orleans Jazz Club here in San Francisco. You really hadn't been too much in contact with that scene here, the kind of traditional jazz scene. Even though there were a lot of traditional players around San Francisco, Pops Foster and Darnell Howard. But about five or six years ago, suddenly you went back and started playing traditional jazz. How did that happen?
